items.question: How certain and swift is the attainment of accomplishment?
premises: Accomplishment arises quickly.
This outcome is affirmed as truth twice.
No doubt exists regarding this.
items.inference: The promised accomplishment is swift and absolutely certain.
items.plain_english: Accomplishment comes quickly indeed; it is truth, truth—there is no doubt.

items.question: Where are the consonants situated according to elemental color?
premises: The goddess of gods is addressed.
Consonants are located in a specific place.
That place is defined by elemental color.
items.inference: The consonants are assigned to the place characterized by that elemental color.
uncertainties: Exact referent of tad bhūta varṇa deśake depends on prior context.
items.plain_english: O goddess of gods, the consonants are in that place of elemental color.

items.question: What should the wise practitioner do with the principal elemental syllable?
premises: A wise practitioner acts.
Each principal elemental syllable is identified.
That syllable is made into Meru.
items.inference: The wise one should arrange each principal elemental syllable as Meru.
uncertainties: The ritual sense of making a syllable into Meru is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Having made that principal elemental syllable into Meru, the wise one proceeds.

items.question: What ritual object is formed from mantra-syllable herb powder?
premises: Powder is made from mantra syllables and herbs.
Pills are made from this powder.
A garland of these pills is used.
items.inference: The practitioner uses a garland made of pills from mantra-syllable herb powder.
uncertainties: Grammatical role of mālayā may be instrumental or associative.
items.plain_english: With a garland made of pills from the powder of mantra syllables and herbs.

items.question: What qualities cause the successful completion of mantra recitation?
premises: Unagitatedness is named.
Non-despair is named.
These are causes of recitation success.
items.inference: Unagitatedness and non-despair bring about success in recitation.
items.plain_english: Unagitatedness and non-despair are the causes of success in recitation.

items.question: What outcome follows proper practice versus improper practice?
premises: One obtains accomplishment in every way under the proper condition.
An alternative condition is stated as otherwise.
Otherwise the result becomes fruitless.
items.inference: Proper practice yields accomplishment, while improper practice yields no fruit.
uncertainties: The specific proper condition is implied from the previous verse.
items.plain_english: In every way one obtains accomplishment; otherwise it would be fruitless.

items.question: How should a practitioner engage in the prescribed ritual action?
premises: That very action is to be performed.
The practitioner should be focused on it in mind.
The practitioner should be devoted to it as the highest aim.
items.inference: One should perform that action with full mental focus and devotion.
items.plain_english: One should perform that very action, with mind fixed on it and devoted to it.

items.question: What qualities must accompany the performance of Vaiṣṇava ritual action?
premises: Vaiṣṇava action is to be worshipfully performed.
The performer must have steadfast intellect.
The performer must have restrained senses.
items.inference: Vaiṣṇava ritual action requires steadfast intellect and restrained senses.
uncertainties: The term vaiṣṇavaṃ karma may reflect a specific ritual context in this text.
items.plain_english: One should perform the Vaiṣṇava rite with steadfast intellect and restrained senses.

items.question: Can accomplishment arise for someone lacking the required qualifications?
premises: Accomplishment is denied even from afar.
This denial applies to the other person.
The best of the twice-born is addressed.
items.inference: For one without the required qualifications, accomplishment does not arise at all.
uncertainties: The identity of itarasya is inferred from contrast with prior verses.
items.plain_english: O best of the twice-born, for the other person accomplishment would not arise, even from afar.

items.question: What daily observances and avoidances are prescribed for the practitioner?
premises: Bathing at three times daily is prescribed.
Small rites are to be avoided.
Both are stated as regular disciplines.
items.inference: The practitioner should bathe thrice daily and avoid minor rites.
items.plain_english: Daily bathing at the three times, and avoidance of petty rites.

items.question: What occasional practice and attitude are required of the practitioner?
premises: Occasional worship is prescribed.
Faith is prescribed.
Faith is directed toward guru and deity.
items.inference: The practitioner must perform occasional worship and maintain faith in guru and deity.
items.plain_english: Occasional worship, and indeed faith in the guru and the deity.

items.question: What mental and practical qualities support effective ritual practice?
premises: Resolve is named as a quality.
Determination is named as a quality.
Completion of the rite is named as a quality.
items.inference: Effective practice requires resolve, determination, and completion of rites.
items.plain_english: Resolve, determination, and indeed the completion of the rite.

items.question: How many defining marks characterize the prescribed discipline here?
premises: Reversed celibacy is included.
This set is identified as a whole.
The whole is described as having eight marks.
items.inference: The prescribed discipline is characterized by eight marks including reversed celibacy.
uncertainties: The meaning of viparītaṃ brahmacaryam is context-specific and unclear.
items.plain_english: Reversed celibacy—this indeed is the set of eight marks.

items.question: What kind of recitation is defined as the regular daily practice?
premises: Recitation is performed every day.
This daily recitation is singled out.
It is traditionally remembered as the regular recitation.
items.inference: Recitation done every day is defined as the regular recitation.
items.plain_english: What one recites every day—this is remembered as the regular recitation.

items.question: On which occasions is recitation classified as occasional rather than regular?
premises: The twelfth day is specified.
The full-moon day is specified.
Recitation on those occasions is called occasional.
items.inference: Recitation performed on the twelfth day and full-moon day is occasional recitation.
uncertainties: teṣu is masculine plural while referring to feminine occasions; taken as general locative reference.
items.plain_english: On the twelfth day and on the full-moon day, the recitation is occasional.

items.question: What attitude should the practitioner adopt after receiving blessing?
premises: Blessing should always be received.
A subsequent action is prescribed.
That action is the practice of contentment.
items.inference: After receiving blessing, the practitioner should cultivate contentment.
items.plain_english: Therefore one should always accept blessing, and then practice contentment.

items.question: What becomes possible in the world when the guru is well pleased?
premises: Nothing is said to be impossible in this world.
This holds when the guru is well pleased.
The sage is addressed.
items.inference: When the guru is well pleased, nothing in the world remains impossible.
uncertainties: guro may be read as vocative or as part of a locative construction with suprasanne.
items.plain_english: O sage, when the guru is well pleased, nothing in this world is impossible.

items.question: With which mantras should the practitioner bathe afterwards?
premises: Bathing is prescribed afterwards.
The bathing uses mantras.
Those mantras are spoken in Veda, Smṛti, and Purāṇa.
items.inference: Afterwards one should bathe using mantras declared in Veda, Smṛti, and Purāṇa.
items.plain_english: Afterwards one should bathe with mantras declared in the Vedas, Smṛtis, and Purāṇas.

items.question: What kind of food is permitted for daily consumption?
premises: Eating is prescribed daily.
Bulbs, roots, and fruits are mentioned.
These are presented as permissible food.
items.inference: One should eat daily using bulbs, roots, and fruits.
items.plain_english: One should eat daily with bulbs, roots, and fruits.

items.question: What mental purity and ethical restraint are required of the mantra practitioner?
premises: The mantra practitioner should be pure-minded.
Harmful conduct is mentioned.
Harmful conduct must not be performed.
items.inference: The mantra practitioner must maintain pure-mindedness and avoid causing harm.
items.plain_english: The mantra practitioner should be pure-minded and should not commit harm.

items.question: What reciprocal effect follows from being favorable toward cows?
premises: Cows are pleased daily.
The cowherd is mentioned.
The cowherd also becomes pleased.
items.inference: When cows are pleased, the cowherd likewise becomes pleased.
uncertainties: The analogy's ritual application is implied rather than explicit.
items.plain_english: When the cows are pleased daily, the cowherd also becomes pleased.

items.question: Which tree shadows must the wise practitioner avoid stepping on?
premises: Stepping on a shadow is prohibited.
The wise one is the subject of the rule.
The shadows are of bibhītaka and karañja trees.
items.inference: The wise practitioner must not step on the shadows of bibhītaka and karañja trees.
items.plain_english: The wise one should not step on the shadow of the bibhītaka and karañja trees.

items.question: Which bodily practice and foods must the practitioner avoid?
premises: Oil anointing is prohibited.
Honey is to be avoided.
Meat is to be avoided.
items.inference: The practitioner must avoid oil anointing, honey, and meat.
items.plain_english: One should not perform oil anointing, and should avoid honey and meat.

items.question: What states and entertainments must the practitioner avoid?
premises: Being naked is prohibited.
Being richly perfumed is prohibited.
Song and instrumental music are to be avoided.
items.inference: The practitioner must avoid nakedness, heavy fragrance, and musical entertainment.
uncertainties: gītavādye is taken as dual object of avoidance despite form ambiguity.
items.plain_english: One should not be naked, nor richly perfumed, and should avoid song and instrumental music.
